requirement:
`OutlineItem::span` covers the item and every attachment it owns, including
leading and trailing attachments. Selecting the item returns the contiguous
source slice covered by that span.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.item_span`. I read the two implementation sites to see what the tests need to exercise. `Outline::from_legacy` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs` widens each item's span with `min(start)` and `max(end)` over its attachments. `validate_outline` in the same file rejects any attachment that lies outside its item's span.

The requirement has two obligations: the item's span covers the item and every attachment it owns, leading and trailing, and selecting the item returns the contiguous slice of that span.

- **Leading and trailing attachments, with selection (Rust).** `search_in_leading_and_trailing_comments_selects_the_function` uses the source `// note before\npub fn check() {} // note after\nfn next() {}`. It selects `fn[check]` and asserts the text is exactly `// note before\npub fn check() {} // note after` after `trim_end()`. That covers both ends of the span and the contiguous slice. It also asserts that `header_span` is still `pub fn check() {`, so the widened span doesn't disturb the item's own spans. It shows the neighbouring `fn next()` is not included.
- **Trailing comment and span value (YAML).** `yaml_selection_includes_comments_owned_by_the_entry` selects `pair[key]` with a trailing comment and asserts the selected text includes it. It also asserts that `outline().items[1].span` equals `Span::new(0, text.len())`, which checks the span value directly rather than only the text. A second case with `# before next\nd: 2` checks that a leading comment is included. In the same case, `pair[a]` correctly excludes the comment that belongs to `d`. A nested `pair[a]/pair[b]` selection is also checked.
- **Leading annotations (Python).** `python_selected_source_includes_its_decorators` asserts the selected text includes the decorator, and that the item's span starts at 0. A second case with two classes named `Checked` and different decorators checks that each selection starts with its own decorator, so a decorator isn't attributed to the wrong item.
- **Span must contain attachments (custom language).** `custom_attachment_spans_are_checked_against_the_original_snapshot` builds a custom outline in which an attachment extends past the item (`Span(1,4)` against an item of `(1,3)`) or starts before it (`Span(0,3)`). It asserts that both are rejected. This checks the invariant that an item's span covers all of its attachments. It also checks that a valid attachment lies within the span.

Together the tests cover leading and trailing attachments, comment and annotation attachment kinds, several languages, and the selection slice. They also check the value of the span itself and the rejection of an outline whose span doesn't cover its attachments. Both extension directions, `min` on start and `max` on end, are exercised. No scenario the requirement names is untested. There are no acknowledgments, and none are needed.
